Narrative
fields.value:
This building is an elementary school with grades K-5. The building is a one story ISO 4 building with brick veneer. The building has classrooms, a kitchen, a cafeteria, a gym, a common library, and common hallways.

There are also small wood framed portable structures on site that function as overflow classrooms. The school was built in the early 1990's according to county GIS information.

Maintenance and housekeeping:
The building is maintained by a full time building operations manager that is at the building daily from opening till closing. Any maintenance or repairs that cannot be completed by the building operations manager is deferred to the maintenance technicians that are employed by the school district and are on call to take care of the buildings owned by the school district. Each evening the building is cleaned by custodians. During the summer months large capital improvements, and maintenance repairs are completed when school is not in session. The overall maintenance and housekeeping are good. No major maintenance issues or deferred maintenance was observed. There are a few minor recommendations that were noted and will be listed in detail in the report. Annually the insured tours the building with a team of maintenance personnel and an annual list of capital improvements or larger maintenance items are noted. There is also a standardized check list that the on site building operator uses to inspect the property on a monthly basis. Work orders are submitted on a daily basis as needed and are computerized and stored online through the insured network.

General hazards and controls:
There is a custodial room that is used to store limited hand tools, equipment, and cleaning supplies. The supplies are stored in open shelving in the custodial room. The door is locked and only the building's operations manager and technicians have access.Flammable solvents were observed in the custodial rooms, consistent with what's needed for small repairs. The amount of flammable liquid was minimal.


There is a kitchen with convection ovens to service the cafeteria. There is no deep frying and no standard grease producing appliances associated with the cooking activity in the main kitchen. Hood cleaning is done semi-annually, which seems appropriate given the cooking hazards present. No type K extinguisher in the kitchen.

The electrical room has storage items blocking full access which should be removed to ensure access and to prevent the area from becoming a defacto storage location for potentially combustible items.

Exterior housekeeping and grounds keeping are good.

Protection:
The building is equipped with fire sprinkler systems, a manual pull down fire alarm, as well as third party monitoring. Fire and smoke detectors were observed. Fire extinguishers were stationed throughout the building.

Security:
Interior and exterior cameras are located in the common areas. There is a staff member that has access to the computer and monitors activity during the day. Sign in is required at the office. There is a third party monitored security system armed after hours. On-call staff are alerted if it is activated. The insured also has its own security staff that are on call during school hours and patrol the area on a regular schedule. If needed they can be dispatched to various locations.

Age of building systems:
All building systems were updated in 2008 as part of a major renovation. No issues with building systems were noted during the survey.

Losses:
A freeze event caused a pipe to burst in the office area. The damage has been repaired, and additional freeze controls have been put in place by the insured.

Overall opinion:
The risk overall is well maintained. The staff appears to be diligent in caring for the buildings. In general after touring the facilities, most of the observations are for minor housekeeping issues, especially storage of items in utility areas. The insured representative was very attentive to loss control and appears willing to comply with recommendations as needed.

fields.label: 4. Type of stucco, if any (if building is stucco-clad, include CLOSE-UP INTERIOR PHOTOS showing the depth of window and/or door openings)?
5. If EIFS-clad, is it a Face-sealed (barrier) EIFS Assembly or a Drainable EIFS Assembly?
fields.help: Instructions A Face-sealed EIFS Assembly is a total barrier system, using caulk or other sealant to prevent water from getting behind the stucco. The problem with this system is that, given the typically high number of joints and other openings, including vents, the likelihood of seal failure is high (either from defective application or eventual sealant breakdown) and, with that, water frequently becomes trapped, leading to moisture-related mold &/or dry rot. A Drainable EIFS Assembly, on the other hand, includes water channels, whereby any water that may get behind the stucco, can escape, thus avoiding any moisture-related mold &/or dry rot problems. As part of your EIFS inspection, look for water channels &/or metal weep screeds (with weep holes for water escape, on the underside) at the exposed bottom of the stucco application. Especially important is that the stucco does not extend all the way to the ground, where it (as well as the weep screed) can be covered by mulch or dirt.

fields.label: 28. Is risk free of Federal Pacific Electric (FPE) Stab-Lok type electrical panels & circuit breakers- MOVE CURSOR OVER TEXT FOR DETAILS (if No, provide a CLOSE-UP PHOTO SHOWING "STAB-LOK" ON THE LABEL?
fields.help: Instructions Federal Pacific Electric (FPE) Stab-Lok type electric panels have a history of breakers not tripping when they should. Due to design or other problems, two-pole FPE Stab-Lok circuit breakers (the type that would feed clothes dryers, for example) do not always work reliably, and, in some studies, they have been noted to fail 30% or more of the time. Identifying an FPE Stab-Lok panel is easy. Simply look for Federal Pacific & the Stab-Lok logo either on the inside or outside of the panel door.

fields.label: 29. Is risk free of GTE-Sylvania Zinsco circuit breaker panels- MOVE CURSOR OVER TEXT FOR DETAILS (if No, provide a CLOSE-UP PHOTO SHOWING "Zinsco" or "GTE-Sylvania" anywhere on the label?
fields.help: Instructions GTE-Sylvania Zinsco breakers have a history of breakers not tripping when they should. The problem is that the circuit breakers inside many Zinsco panels melt to the main �bus bar�, rendering the breaker unable to trip, even when there�s a short or overloaded circuit, with the net result, given a surge of power, wires melt and a fire ensues. Identifying a GTE-Sylvania Zinsco breaker is easy. Simply look for the "GTE-Sylvania" &/or "Zinsco" label anywhere on the panel. Additionally, Zinsco breakers have color-coded toggle switches (15 amps blue; 20 amp red or orange; 30 amp green; 40 amp grey).

fields.label: 30. Is risk free of extension cord overuse?
fields.help: Instructions Extension cords should never be permanently coonected to large appliances e.g. a refrigerator or an air conditioning unit.

13. Does risk have at least two means of egress per floor, including the basement, should the basement house apartments or commercial occupancies (if No, explain)?
fields.help: Instructions While the two remote means of egress rule, namely, "There shall be at least two independent exits, remote from each other, from every floor of a building", exceptions that allow only one exit include one & two family dwellings, buildings of not more than 3 stories, with one family per floor and with the egress stairway sprinklered (in other words, your typical "brownstone"), and as frequently found in NYC and elsewhere, small two story mixed use masonry buildings having one or two 2nd floor apartments with egress stairway separated from first floor occupancy and leading directly to the street.

fields.label: 14. If only one means of egress from an upper floor or occupied basement, is the stairway sprinklered?
15. Is access to exits unobstructed and with outward opening exit doors/egress passage doorways?
16. Do exit doors/egress passage doorways have illuminated exit signs (with directional arrows, as required- MOVE CURSOR OVER THIS TEXT TO VIEW THE CODE REQUIREMENT)?
fields.help: Instructions All exits and access ways must be marked by an approved exit sign which is visible & distinguishable from any egress travel path. Every exit sign must be illuminated by a reliable light source. In new buildings, sign placement must be such that no point in the exit access is more than 100 ft from the nearest visible sign. Exception: Main exterior exit doors that are clearly visible & identifiable as exits (e.g. small mercantiles with glass front doors, as with most dry cleaning drop-off stations, Chinese take-outs & the like).

fields.label: 17. Is premises ADA (Americans with Disabilities Act)-compliant?
fields.help: Instructions Regarding Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) compliance, we are mostly concerned that, per the Act, "people with disabilities should be able to arrive on the site, approach the building, and enter as freely as everyone else. At least one route of travel should be safe and accessible for everyone, including people with disabilities.". That amounts to accessibility for wheelchair-bound individuals, either by a door at grade (not requiring a step-up) or by a wheelchair ramp, in both cases, wide enough to accommodate a wheelchair. Note that this mostly applies to public and other buildings. e.g. a school, a library, etc., where services & events are for the general public and where not affording equal access could be construed as discriminatory . And while full ADA compliance extends, for example, to rest rooms, etc., we pretty much limit our concern to accessing and exiting a building and any rec we make should be site specific, in that regard.

fields.label: 18. Are emergency exit doors equipped with working panic hardware (N/A, if not required)?
19. Is working emergency lighting provided (N/A, if not required- MOVE CURSOR OVER THIS TEXT TO VIEW THE CODE REQUIREMENT)?
fields.help: Instructions Required in apartment buildings of 12 units or more, or more than three stories in height, unless every dwelling unit has a direct exit to the outside of the building at grade. Also required in commercial spaces, including mercantiles, of more than 3,000sf. And typically places of assembly of more than 50 people (an exception being churches of less than 300 assembled).

fields.label: 20. If building is elevatored, are the elevators on a service contract, have a posted current inspection and appear in good working order & free of observed deficiencies (if No, describe)?
21. Are all stairways in good condition and to NFPA Life Safety 101 requirements, including continuous, graspable handrails and non-slip tread coverings, as necessary (if No, FULLY detail)?
fields.help: Instructions Following a recent high six figure claim involving a stairway fall injury incurred by a restaurant patron on his way to a basement rest room, our largest client strongly reminded us of the importance of fully documenting issues involving stairway handrails, step treads, including tread traction, riser heights and lighting. As it was, the stairway in question, had a noticeable gap between the upper & lower railings, which is where the injured patron, on attempting to grab it, fell down the stairs. The building code calls for continuous, graspable handrails, something that was not in place. Additionally, the step risers were also out of code, at over 9 inches high (risers should all be of uniform height, not exceeding 7 inches). On top of that, the report photos, besides not documenting the subject stairway, were also blurry, with our client further underscoring the need for an adequate number of high resolution stairway photos, in all of our reports. Your diligence, in addressing these concerns, is of utmost importance and greatly appreciated.

fields.label: 1. Do inspected apartments (vacant &/or occupied) entry doors self-close and latch properly (if No, detail)?

fields.help: Instructions Note: The magnet is de-energized (and no longer holds) when a fire alarm is sounded or the building loses power.

fields.label: 6. Do all auto-closing doors become self-closing upon release of thehold-open mechanism and that the releasing mechanism is activated by smoke detection, including upon loss of power to the smoke detection device?
fields.help: Instructions Under normal conditions, the fire alarm control panel energizes the electromagnet and holds the door open. When smoke is detected anywhere in the building, the alarm panel deenergizes the electromagnets and all of the fire doors in the building swing closed.

fields.label: 7. Do all auto-closing hallway/corridor fire doors employ hold open devices that release other than by smoke detection, instead using fusible links, which on melting when the temperature reaches a certain point, cause the doors to self-close?
fields.help: Instructions On doors with swing hold open mechanisms using a fusible link, one may be able to see the metal link (two small pieces of metal held together by soder) along the swing arm at the top of the door.

fields.label: 8. Do all observed fire stair doors (including those on the first and top floors) self-close and latch properly?
9. Any observed propped open hallway/corridor doors, fire stair doors &/or apartment entry doors (if Yes, locate and provide photos)?
10. Where hallway/corridor doors, fire stair doors &/or apartment entry doors are observed to be propped open, are tenants warned to desist from this practice as it presents a serious safety hazard?
11. How often and by whom are fire doors and apartment entry doors inspected?
12. Are fire doors and apartment entry doors on a regular maintenance schedule (if Yes, detail)?
13. Does risk have scissor-type fire stairs (i.e. two sets of stairways that are intertwined in the center of the hallway, with a wall between them)?
fields.help: Instructions Key with scissor-type stairways is that they discharge at opposite sides of the building core on alternate floors. So, in the case of, for example, a "scissor-type" stairway "A" opening on the North end of floor 10, it would discharge on the South side of floor 8, while not discharging at all on floor 9. In the case of straight-type stairways, they discharge at the same sides of the building core on every floor. So, in the case of, for example, a "straight -type stairway "A" opening on the North end of floor 10, it would discharge on the North end of floor 9 and every other floor above or below.
